description:
Programme or Project Overview

King's College London advertises a funded PhD studentship under reference number 161245. The position is advertised through the university's Corehr recruitment portal, and the closing date is to be confirmed - King's studentship competitions of this type typically close around December, so early preparation is strongly advised. Funded studentships at King's cover tuition fees at the home or international rate specified in the advert and provide an annual tax-free stipend at the UKRI doctoral rate for the duration of the studentship.

Because the direct job-specification link may not resolve for all browsers, applicants should open the King's College London careers portal and search for 'PhD Studentship 161245' to reach the full advertisement, person specification and application form. The listing carries the definitive eligibility rules, project description and supervisory team, and applications are submitted through the portal with references and transcripts uploaded directly.

How to apply

Create an applicant profile on the KCL recruitment portal, search for the reference number, and follow the application instructions on the advertisement. Prepare a CV, degree transcripts, two academic references and a research statement before starting the form, and check the advert for any additional questions specific to this studentship. Where a closing date is not yet shown, candidates are advised to monitor the portal and to note that complete applications are required before the published deadline - late or partial submissions cannot be considered.

  • Funded PhD studentship at King's College London
  • Reference number 161245 on the KCL careers portal
  • UKRI-rate annual stipend and fee support per the advert
  • Central London research environment

About King's College London

King's College London is a public research university and a Russell Group member. Its undergraduate, postgraduate and doctoral programmes span medicine, law, humanities, psychology, science and other disciplines. With campuses across central London, King's connects academic study and research with healthcare institutions, cultural organisations and wider questions affecting contemporary society.
